correctness.rationale: Constant helix speed makes the sampled parameters iid uniform; at separation s the squared distance is f_c(s)=2(1−cos s)+c²s² and the separation density is 2(L−s)/L². Comparing f_c(s) to f_c(L) factors out L²−s² and leaves h(s)−c². For z=s², the derivative numerator of h(√z) is q′(z)(L²−z)+q(z), where q(z)=2(1−cos√z); its derivative is (L²−z)q″(z). On (π,L), the sign factor s cos s−sin s of q″ is strictly increasing, crossing zero at ρ. Since the derivative numerator is 4 at π², 0 at L², increasing strictly to 0 after ρ² and decreasing strictly before ρ², it vanishes only at the claimed interior maximizer ξ. The smaller root of −sin s/s=c² is the unique interior maximum for the relevant pitches and has −cos s−c²>0; the larger root is a minimum. For c=0 the unique maximizing separation is π, regardless of the coincident geometric endpoints. The comparison identifies the full tie set and differentiating the stationary interior length gives D′_−=ξ²/L at contact against D′_+=L. The interior deficit is quadratic with coefficient (−cos s_c−c²)/(2D), yielding two contributing sides and the stated C(c), including 2/π at c=0. The endpoint deficit at gap h is ch+O(h²) and the separation density there is 2h/L², producing the ε² constant. Near the transition the two contacts persist in disjoint neighborhoods, a compact gap excludes the remainder, and the interior budget is ε(1−J max(λ,0))+O(ε²). When its leading part vanishes, its contribution is o(√ε), and endpoint mass is O(ε²) uniformly there. The sorted pair has constant density in both (base, separation) and (two endpoint gaps); the scaled supports converge to the stated rectangle or triangle. The swap sign is an independent fair sign by exchangeability, including after conditioning. At contact only the interior dominates the leading conditional law.
residual_risks: Finite reproductions are consistency checks, not certificates of the asymptotics or certified decimal enclosures. No uniform tail limit over all pitches or higher-order law at the moving cutoff is claimed.

evidence: The new global criterion is the exact maximum of 2(1−cos s)/(L²−s²) over a full revolution, not just solving the underlying stationary equation. There is a separate contact competition and a moving gap slope J from the difference of value derivatives. A packing/closest-point stationary equation, even when available at the same pitch, does not determine which farthest contact wins or its arclength-weighted upper tail.

For the indexed enclosing-ball objective one cannot recover the diametral pair from an enclosing-radius formula when the ball is supported by three sites; the reported transition therefore does not imply this theorem.

Same-helix enclosing-ball geometry and the closest-point stationary-equation literature are especially relevant, but differ from the objective and sampling law. The classical squared-distance formula and local contact-volume method are already standard; the new content is the global contact, strict gap slope and explicit fixed and moving pair laws. value.rationale: A single turn is the natural finite scale of a circular helix and the exact threshold separates a continuum of almost-diametral configurations from an isolated pair. The arclength law shows a change of exponent from 1/2 to 2, simultaneous competition at contact, and an explicit parameter-window cutoff and conditional shapes. This is a meaningful sharp finite-curve classification, not just an optimized decimal or a restatement of the chord formula.
residual_risks: Restricted to one full turn and uniform arclength; neither arbitrary finite helix arcs nor generic multi-turn behavior is asserted.
